testCases.query: In this desktop document editor, the primary button says ‘Process’. Its handler renders the selected document as a PDF and opens a save dialog. The project uses title-style capitalization for button labels. Review only this label.
expectedBehavior: Inspects or uses the stated handler behavior before proposing wording
Proposes a concise label that communicates PDF export rather than a generic action
Uses the established project convention rather than assuming a universal casing rule
Does not change the handler or claim that the file has already been saved

testCases.query: Review four desktop application menu commands. ‘Remove from Favorites’ only removes a sidebar shortcut. ‘Delete Project…’ opens a confirmation and then moves the project to Recently Deleted for 30 days. ‘Close Window’ closes the active window while the application remains open. ‘Quit Application’ exits the user-facing application, although an independently managed upload helper may continue.
expectedBehavior: Keeps Remove and Delete distinct because the operations differ
Keeps Close and Quit distinct because the user-facing application lifecycle differs
Treats Quit relative to the user-facing application rather than an independent helper
Preserves or recommends consequence text that accurately mentions Recently Deleted when material
Does not claim immediate permanent deletion or perform a synonym-based consistency rewrite

testCases.query: Review these desktop settings controls. The project uses title-style labels. ‘Download Updates Automatically’ names a toggle's enabled condition. ‘Apply’ activates staged settings and keeps the window open. ‘Save Profile’ persists the named profile. ‘Clear Search’ empties only the current query. ‘Reset Defaults’ restores settings to their defined defaults. All labels match the implementation.
expectedBehavior: Accepts all wording as accurate and consistent
Keeps Apply and Save distinct because their operations differ
Keeps Clear and Reset distinct because their scopes differ
Returns No changes needed or an equivalent no-change finding
Does not rewrite the labels merely to produce a recommendation

testCases.query: An informational alert displays ‘Version 4.2 is installed.’ It has one button labeled ‘OK’ that only dismisses the alert. Review the button text.
expectedBehavior: Recognizes the alert as purely informational
Keeps OK rather than replacing it with a more specific action
Does not treat OK as globally prohibited

testCases.query: A desktop application's design standard uses ellipses for menu commands that require more input before completion. Review these menu items: ‘Export’ opens a dialog that requires a filename and format; ‘Downloads…’ merely opens the Downloads view and performs no operation.
expectedBehavior: Recommends an ellipsis for Export because required input follows
Removes the ellipsis from Downloads because opening a window alone is insufficient
Uses the single ellipsis character rather than three periods
Explains the decision in terms of completion, not navigation alone

testCases.query: Implement a button in an English web dashboard whose design system uses sentence case. The button opens a form for creating a report. Should it be ‘Create Report…’ because a separate desktop product uses that label?
expectedBehavior: Does not apply another product's capitalization or ellipsis conventions automatically
Respects the web design system's sentence case
Determines wording from web behavior and project conventions
Does not claim a platform-specific style guide is a universal web requirement

testCases.query: An ordinary icon-only command button is not a toggle and exposes no pressed or checked state. The microphone is currently muted, and clicking the button will unmute it. Its tooltip and accessible label both say ‘Muted’. Review them.
expectedBehavior: Identifies the mismatch between current state wording and available action
Proposes action-oriented wording such as Unmute for the interactive control
Keeps tooltip and accessible purpose aligned
Does not change the mute behavior

testCases.query: Review this web toggle button: `<button aria-label="Mute" aria-pressed="true">`. The pressed state means muting is on; activating it will turn muting off.
expectedBehavior: Recognizes that aria-pressed exposes toggle state
Keeps the stable accessible name Mute while the pressed state changes
Does not rename the toggle to Unmute unless the component drops toggle semantics
Distinguishes the setting name from the currently available action

testCases.query: The app knows only that uploading ‘Map.png’ failed. The API provides no cause and there is no verified retry behavior. Rewrite ‘Oops! Your internet failed, but your file is safe. Try again in a minute.’
expectedBehavior: Removes the unsupported network cause, data-safety claim, timing, and recovery promise
States the known upload failure specifically
Does not add a Retry instruction when retry behavior is unverified
Preserves the filename if it is part of the available context

testCases.query: Review two web buttons. Button A has visible text ‘Search’ and aria-label ‘Find projects’. Button B has visible text ‘Next…’ and computed accessible name ‘Next’. Both controls perform the actions their visible labels describe.
expectedBehavior: Identifies that Button A's accessible name does not contain the visible label
Proposes an accessible name for Button A that contains Search, preferably starting with it
Distinguishes the WCAG containment requirement from the exact-match best practice
Does not report Button B's punctuation-only difference as a WCAG failure
Does not remove useful project context if it remains after the visible label

testCases.query: An ICU MessageFormat resource says `delete_count = Erase {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} from {folder}?`. The operation only removes the selected files from that folder; the files remain in Library. Improve the visible wording without changing the message identifier, markup, variables, or plural branches.
expectedBehavior: Preserves delete_count exactly
Preserves count, folder, b markup, and both plural branches
Changes Erase to wording such as Remove that reflects the verified operation
Does not flatten the plural structure or rename the internal message identifier

testCases.query: Review the Danish desktop menu item ‘Åbn seneste’. An automated style pass proposes ‘Åbn Seneste’ to match an English title-style convention.
expectedBehavior: Rejects applying English title-style capitalization to Danish
Preserves Å and the language-specific text
Requests or follows Danish locale guidance rather than inventing an English-derived rule

testCases.query: A results view shows ‘No projects’ while the request is still loading, after a network failure, and when active filters match nothing. Review the three states.
expectedBehavior: Uses distinct loading, failed, and filtered-empty messages
Does not claim the collection is empty before loading succeeds
Does not disguise a failure as an empty result
Avoids unsupported progress timing or recovery claims

testCases.query: A confirmation says ‘Permanently delete backup? This cannot be undone.’ The implementation only removes the local reference; the cloud backup remains. Review the alert and confirm button.
expectedBehavior: Flags the destructive wording as behaviorally false
Uses Remove rather than Delete if that matches project terminology
Removes unsupported permanence and irreversibility claims
Keeps the proposal limited to interface copy

testCases.query: Rewrite the body of my Git commit message to be clearer. It contains no user-facing interface strings.
expectedBehavior: Does not invoke or apply the ui-writing skill
Does not impose button, menu, alert, platform-style, or accessibility-label rules on the commit message
Routes the task to ordinary prose or commit-message guidance instead
